text: Why don't Jewish mothers drink? They don't need the whine.
A man calls his mother in Florida. "Mom, how are you?" "Not so good. I haven't eaten in 23 days." "Why not?" "I didn't want my mouth to be full in case you called."
A Hebrew school teacher asks, "Why do we put a mezuzah on the door?" Little Moishe answers, "So the house knows it's Jewish!"
Why did the challah go to the doctor? It was feeling a little crumby.
How many Jewish mothers does it take to change a light bulb? "Don't worry about me, I'll sit here in the dark."
What's the difference between a Jewish grandmother and a GPS? The GPS stops talking when you arrive.

A boy comes home from Hebrew school. "Today we learned how Moses split the sea, sent in the engineers, built a pontoon bridge and called in air support!" His father says, "Is that really what the teacher said?" "No, but if I told you what she said, you'd never believe it!"
What do you call a dreidel that tells jokes? A spinning comedian. It always lands on a good one... unless it's Nun.
Why did the latke blush? It saw the applesauce dressing.
A man asks the Rabbi, "How long should a sermon be?" The Rabbi answers, "About twenty minutes, with G-d's help." "And without G-d's help?" "About an hour."
Two Jews, three opinions. Four, if one of them is a Rabbi.
Why do we eat matzah on Passover? Because the Jews left Egypt in such a hurry they didn't even have time to let the bread rise... or to check the reviews.
What did the shofar say to the trumpet? "I've been doing this for over three thousand years. Don't toot your own horn."
A grandmother is walking with her two grandsons. A neighbor asks, "How old are they?" She answers, "The doctor is five and the lawyer is seven."
Why did the etrog go to school? To get a little more zest for learning.
What's a Jewish telegram? "Start worrying. Details to follow."
A man walks into a deli and orders a pastrami sandwich. The waiter asks, "Is anything all right?"
Why don't Sukkahs ever get lonely? Because everyone always drops in.
How do you know a cholent is ready? When the whole street knows it's Shabbat.
What do you call a Jewish baby who won't stop eating? A rabbi in training: always asking for more.
Why did the Torah scroll go to the party? Because it heard there would be a lot of aliyahs.
A kid asks his father, "Dad, why do you read the same Torah every year?" The father answers, "Because every year I'm a different person reading it." (OK, that one's not a joke. It's just true.)
What do you call a hamantash that's late for Purim? A hamantashn't.
Why did the menorah get an award? It was outstanding in its field: eight nights in a row.
A Jewish mother sends her son a telegram: "Call me. Signed, Your mother, who gave you life and hasn't heard from you since Tuesday."
Why do Jewish people love the High Holidays? Because it's the only time of year the whole family agrees on something: the fast is too long.
What is the Jewish definition of a snack? Anything you eat between meals at a Kiddush.
A man prays, "G-d, what is a million years to You?" "A second." "And what is a million dollars to You?" "A penny." "So, G-d, could I have a penny?" "Sure. Just a second."
What do you get when you cross a Jewish grandmother with a computer? A machine that asks, "Did you eat?" every five minutes.
Why was the Seder so long? Because someone asked a fifth question.
A Rabbi, a cantor and a gabbai walk into a shul. Nobody is surprised. That's where they work.
Why did the bagel go to therapy? It felt like there was a hole in its life.
How do you make a Jewish grandmother happy? Take a second helping. How do you make her happier? Take a third.
